groups.title: Server to React
groups.text: The data is in the HTML before the first paint: PHP gathers it, PAD writes it into the page, React picks it up. No second request, no loading spinner.

groups.title: React back to PAD
groups.text: The component asks the server again while it runs - the same pages answer JSON, a single fragment, or take a post - and PAD stays the one that knows.

groups.title: React basics
groups.text: State, events, forms and composition - plain React, mounted in a PAD page.

examples.title: Islands with props
examples.lede: PHP prepares the data, the ^ sigil writes a field as JSON into a data attribute, and one small runtime mounts a component on every island of the page - each with its own state.

examples.title: Progressive enhancement
examples.lede: PAD renders a complete table - with JavaScript off it is all there. React then takes the same element over and adds search and sorting, and can show you what the server sent.

examples.title: Data files with a tag
examples.lede: A custom tag of the application reads _data/products.json and writes it into a data attribute; a product grid filters and sorts it in the browser. Bare React, no runtime.

examples.title: Providers with {reactData}
examples.lede: Four providers in _providers/ query the database, each building on the one before it; {reactData} writes every answer as a mount point and React draws the forum topic.

examples.title: One page, two answers
examples.lede: The page renders HTML for the browser and answers JSON to fetch(): the same PHP filters, sorts and pages the catalogue, and $padExpose names what may leave the server.

examples.title: Forms checked by PAD
examples.lede: One list of rules for both sides: the browser checks the form with them first, then React posts it with the session's CSRF token in a header and padValidate answers a message per field, or the new list of messages.

examples.title: Islands sharing server state
examples.lede: Two islands, one cart kept in the PHP session: the shelf posts, the server answers the cart, and an event tells the other island - a reload shows the same cart.

examples.title: PAD draws, React steers
examples.lede: React holds the controls; PAD renders the {chart} as SVG and answers just that {fragment}. The first chart is in the HTML before any script ran.

examples.title: Live polling
examples.lede: A status board asks its page for fresh JSON every few seconds and stops while the tab is hidden; padCache counts the asks of every visitor.

examples.title: Counter with history
examples.lede: The start value comes from PHP in a data attribute; the step size, the undo history and the statistics are React state.

examples.title: Composition
examples.lede: Small components - a card, a button, a todo item - put together into bigger ones with props and children.

examples.title: Controlled form
examples.lede: Every field is React state and checked as you type - nothing leaves the browser. Compare it with the form PAD checks.

examples.title: Toggles
examples.lede: A switch component used three times - each copy keeps its own state.

examples.title: Click handler
examples.lede: An event handler that reads where you clicked and leaves a ripple there.
